div.head: THE COW.

lg.l: Early the milkmaid to the meadow hies, And the red Cow her empty pail supplies.

div.p:
This is the good-natured Cow to which we are all so much obliged. She comes, poor thing! in the morning, and brings her udder full of milk for
our breakfast, and the same at night for our supper. To her we are indebted for our custards, cheesecakes, curds, and cream, as well as for our milk, butter, and cheese.

div.head: THE NIGHTINGALE.

lg.l: The Nightingale doth sweetly sing, To welcome in the cheerful spring.

div.p: What a pretty bird the Nightingale is! How sweetly she sings! I could wish 'twas summer all the year for the sake of her good company.

div.head: THE LAMB.

lg.l: The little Lamb doth skip and play, Always merry, always gay.

div.p: See the little Lamb! how innocent he looks! he never did any harm, and therefore is beloved by every body: but the fox and the wolf, who are always in mischief, are hated and despised.

div.head: THE LION.

lg.l: The Lion ranges round the wood, And makes the lesser beasts his food: Thus tyrants on their subject prey, And rule with arbitrary sway.

div.p:
Though the Lion is such a strong devouring creature, yet Daniel was thrown into a den among several of
them, and received no harm. For he was punished on account of his religion and virtue, he prayed unto God, and the Lord delivered him.

div.head: THE WHALE.

lg.l: The Whale's the monarch of the main, (As is the Lion of the plain:) He keeps the lesser fish in awe, And, tyrant-like, his will's his law.

div.p:
When the prophet Jonah attempted to fly over sea from the presence of the Lord, there arose a great storm, and
he being cast into the deep, was swallowed by this great fish, in whose belly he repented sincerely, and prayed unto God; wherefore the Lord commanded the fish, and he swam to shore, and cast him upon dry land.
